source.stem:
The diameter of a copper wire is thought to be approximately 0.3 mm.
Which instrument should be used to obtain a more accurate measurement of the diameter of the wire?

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: 120 m in 20 s is faster than 100 m in 10 s.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: 40 m in 10 s is faster than 60 m in 10 s.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Cannot compare 60 m in 10 s with 60 m in 15 s because the times differ.

intelligence.enrichment: For the same time interval, the object that covers more distance is faster; for different distances or times, compare distance covered in unit time, which is speed. More distance in the same time, or more distance per unit time, means a higher speed. The learner correctly applies this rule: For the same time interval, the object that covers more distance is faster; for different distances or times, compare distance covered in unit time, which is speed. The faster object is whichever has the larger distance number or the smaller time number, without comparing distance per unit time.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 7 Science question. Chapter: Measurement of time. The student must decide: Compare which object is faster from distance and time information. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key.
